claims.claim: The resignation came as the company had not yet closed a $13 billion deal to acquire the open‑source platform Hugging Face, and it had just agreed to pay $6 billion for a non‑exclusive license from the AI‑coding start‑up Poolside.
claims.bestSource: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question - TechCrunch
claims.evidence: Without Huang, the concern among open source community members is that whoever takes over will be more cautious. Nvidia has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. It’s not clear how Kress will approach the Hugging Face deal or support for the open model ecosystem, but founder-driven priorities tend to get a downgrade when leadership changes. Huang’s departure also comes as Nvidia has yet to finalize a deal to acquire open source platform Hugging Face for $13 billion . Still, supporting open source isn’t simply a passion project Huang pursued out of idealism. It’s increasingly central to Nvidia’s business strategy. Huang has been a staunch supporter of open source AI, framing the ecosystem as good for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. Huang’s influence extended beyond Nvidia’s investments and product roadmap. He also emerged as one of the most prominent voices pushing back against Washington’s efforts to restrict the open AI ecosystem. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the motives behind the executive’s support for softer chip export controls on China. Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads — potential competitors to closed frontier models. One company insider told TechCrunch that they don’t expect a change in leadership to have an impact on Nemotron development. Nvidia also agreed to pay $6 billion for a non-exclusive license for open AI coding startup Poolside’s technology. The question now is whether that commitment can survive without the man who made it a priority. TechCrunch has reached out to Nvidia for comment.
